transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m here because this has been going on for months, and I can’t get anyone to really see it. My husband’s family, they’ve been quietly interfering with our money and with my reputation. It’s not like they come out and say it, you know? It’s little things.

Like at work, I do billing, and suddenly there are these little errors showing up, things that make me look careless. And then someone at church will act strange toward me, like they heard something. My sister-in-law has always been the kind to smile at you and then… well, anyway. People keep telling me they checked records or it doesn’t prove anything, but I know it all ties back to them somehow.
Aside from these experiences of being targeted, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see?

I don’t… I mean, not like that, no. I haven’t seen some person standing there that nobody else sees or anything. And voices—people keep saying “voices” like I’m making this up, but it’s not that.

It’s more that people act differently, or things happen at work, and you can just tell something’s been said. Like when I was in high school there were girls who could turn a whole room against you without ever saying it to your face, and my sister-in-law has that same way about her. So no, I don’t think I’m hearing things other people can’t hear. It’s not like that.

Over these past few months, have you also noticed any changes in your mood—like periods of feeling unusually high-energy, elated, or irritable, or on the other hand, feeling very depressed or losing interest in things—that lasted several days or more?

I don’t know… I mean, I get upset, sure, because who wouldn’t, with all this hanging over them? But I don’t think of it like moods exactly. Some days I’m more on edge, especially if something happens at work or somebody gives me that look at church.

As far as being really “high” or energetic, no, I don’t think so. Depressed… I mean, I have days where I don’t want to deal with people, but I still go to work, do what I have to do. It’s hard to separate what’s a mood from what’s just reacting to what’s been going on, you know?

Before these past few months, would you say you were generally a trusting person, or have you always tended to be wary and suspicious of other people's motives, even going back to childhood or early adulthood?

I don’t know if I’d call myself suspicious. I mean, I’ve always paid attention to people, you know? My mother used to say I noticed things other people missed, like if somebody’s tone changed or they stopped calling as much. But that doesn’t mean I was walking around thinking everyone was out to get me.

In school I wasn’t… well, girls can be mean, and you learn to watch who you tell things to. And at work, with billing, you have to be careful because one wrong number and suddenly it’s on you. So I guess I’ve always been cautious. But trusting? It depends who. Some people earn it, some people don’t.

If someone showed you clear evidence that your sister-in-law or coworkers had nothing to do with these errors or comments, would that change your mind, or would you still feel certain they were involved?

I mean… if it was real evidence, I’d look at it. I’m not unreasonable. But people keep saying “records” like records can show everything. They can pull up whatever screen at work and say, see, it was just an error, but that doesn’t explain why these little mistakes keep happening around me, or why someone at church suddenly acts strange like they’ve heard something.

And with my husband’s family—especially my sister-in-law—it’s not always something you can put on paper. It’s quiet. It’s the money, our name, little comments that get around. So I don’t know that one printout or someone saying “we checked” would change what I already know is connected.

Before the last few months, did you ever believe that specific people or groups—like coworkers, neighbors, or other family members—were actually organizing against you or trying to harm your reputation in this same deliberate way, or is this the first time you've felt this certain about a specific group being behind it?

No, not like this. I mean, I’ve had issues with people before—everybody has, especially in offices, there’s always someone who wants to make themselves look better. But this… this started maybe nine months ago, around when things got ugly with my husband’s family about money and the holidays. 

That’s when I started feeling like it wasn’t just random little things anymore. Before that, I wouldn’t have said there was a specific group behind anything. I might’ve been cautious, but not certain like I am now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory belief system centered on her husband's family (particularly her sister-in-law) and coworkers colluding against her financially and reputationally, persisting for approximately 9 months. She denies auditory or visual hallucinations, and there is no evidence of manic, hypomanic, or major depressive episodes to suggest a mood disorder with psychotic features. Her overall functioning remains intact (continues working, attending church), arguing against schizophrenia, which requires more pervasive functional decline and typically additional symptoms such as hallucinations, disorganized speech, or negative symptoms. While she describes a longstanding tendency toward vigilance and cautiousness, she denies a lifelong pattern of pervasive distrust and suspicion predating this episode, and the delusional certainty is new and circumscribed to this specific belief system, distinguishing it from paranoid personality disorder. The circumscribed, non-bizarre, single-theme persecutory delusion without hallucinations, mood episodes, or global functional deterioration is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (F22).
